summary: The Sun is exalted in Aries (deepest exaltation at 10°), which gives strong self-confidence, initiative and a drive to lead. Classical texts describe a famous, energetic, combative person who rises through their own effort.
common_outcomes: Strong will, self-reliance and willingness to take the lead
Recognition or fame for skill or bold action
Restless, active temperament; likes travel and movement
Attraction to competitive, military, sporting or command roles
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka says the native is famous and clever but wanders and gains little, and bears weapons when the Sun is not in its exact exaltation degree
Saravali 22.2-3 describes a commentator on scriptures, famous in the arts, who becomes a king or ruler-like figure
Saravali 22.2-3 associates the placement with a 'bilious' (pitta) constitution and strong bones

by_area.personality: Bold, fierce, fond of war and roaming, attached to duty (Saravali 22.2-3); active, ambitious, impulsive, irritable and pioneering (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Saravali 22.2-3 says the native may rise to kingly status; Raman lists warrior and traveller; Brihat Jataka 18.1 says the native bears weapons when the Sun is short of its exact exaltation degree.
by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka 18.1: fame with little gain; Raman: wealthy but of variable fortune; Phaladeepika 9.14 (any exalted planet): wealth and treasures.
by_area.health: Saravali 22.2-3 links the placement to bilious and blood disorders and strong bones; treat as a temperament note only, never as a medical prediction.
by_area.spirituality: Saravali 22.2-3: comments on the meaning of the shastras.

strengtheners: Near 10° Aries (exact exaltation); Brihat Jataka 18.1 specifically distinguishes results at the exaltation degree
Kendra placement; Braha (p. 50) says planets in kendras are powerful and prominent
Placement in the 10th, where the Sun has directional strength (Braha pp. 17, 60)
Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 22.4-9: wealth and high office) or Mars's aspect (courage in battle)
Exalted or own sign in the navamsa, or vargottama (Braha pp. 13-14, 59-60)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saturn's aspect (Saravali 22.4-9: grief, dullness for the Sun in Mars's signs)
Venus's aspect (Saravali lists an unhappy marriage among results for Sun in Mars's signs)
Placement in a dusthana (6th, 8th, 12th); Braha (pp. 51-52) says a planet there is spoiled, the 6th being the mildest
Mercury's aspect: Saravali gives servitude and poverty for the Sun in Mars's signs
lagna_or_context_notes: Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the exalted or own-sign Sun house by house. With the Sun in Aries: Aries lagna (1st) respect, learning and a good start in life; Cancer lagna (10th) fame and a high position; Leo lagna (9th) fortune, faith and a prosperous father; Capricorn lagna (4th) homes, property and power but less happiness from the mother; Gemini lagna (11th) wealth from many sources; Libra lagna (7th) a capable spouse while the Sun's usual 7th-house strains remain.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.49-50
source_views.view: Sun's exaltation sign is Aries at 10°; the 7th sign (Libra) at the same degree is its debilitation.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.1 (tr. M. D. Neely, 2007)
source_views.view: Sun in Aries: famous, clever, wandering, with little gain; bears arms when not at the exaltation degree.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.2-3, Sun in Aries (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Scholarly commentator, famous in the arts, fond of war, fierce, dutiful, wanderer, strong-boned, brave, pitta/blood tendency, radiant and kingly.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.4-9, aspects on the Sun in Mars's signs (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Moon's aspect gives generosity and servants; Mars courage in battle; Mercury servitude; Jupiter wealth and high office; Venus a difficult marriage; Saturn grief and dullness.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 9.14 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: A planet in exaltation gives rule over land, royal praise, wealth, fame, valour, generosity and cleverness.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXII 'Planets in Different Rasis or Signs' (Sun, pp. 204-205)
source_views.view: Active, intelligent, famous, a traveller, wealthy, warrior-like, variable fortune, ambitious, powerful, impulsive, irritable, pioneering.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'Planetary Powers' p. 47 and '1st House' (pp. 79-90)
source_views.view: Sun is exalted in Aries; a planet before its deepest degree keeps the state less intensely and one past it is technically no longer exalted; the exalted Sun in the 1st gives respect, learning and a good start in life.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Surya, the Sun, name 70 ('The victor')
source_views.view: Exaltation in Aries gives a sense of being naturally victorious, peaking at 10 degrees Aries.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'The Sun' p. 17, 'Navamsa' pp. 13-14, 'House Rulerships' pp. 50-52 and 'Shad Bala' pp. 59-61
source_views.view: The Sun does best in the upachaya houses and in the 10th (directional strength); planets in kendras are powerful and in trikonas flourish, while a planet in a dusthana is spoiled; dignity in the navamsa or vargottama strengthens a planet, but not a fallen one.

disagreements: Brihat Jataka gives fame with limited gain and a wandering, weapon-bearing life unless the Sun is at its exact exaltation degree; Saravali is more uniformly positive (kingly), and Raman lists wealth with variable fortune. BPHS 3.49-50 treats all of Aries as exaltation with the peak at 10 degrees, while Braha (p. 47) says a planet past its deepest degree is technically no longer exalted.
phrasing_guidance: Describe as strong confidence and leadership potential that grows with effort. Avoid promising fame or power; note that impatience or pride is the main thing to manage. No health or longevity predictions.

summary: The Sun in Taurus sits in the sign of Venus, a natural enemy, so its fiery assertiveness becomes steadier and more pleasure- and resource-oriented. Texts link it to arts, music, trade in fine goods and enjoyment of comforts.
common_outcomes: Clever and reflective; slow to act but self-confident (Raman HPA ch. XXII)
Interest or skill in singing, music, dance or aesthetic trades
Livelihood through trade in cloth, perfumes or other fine goods
Enjoys food, garments, scents and comforts
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka says the native dislikes women or is at odds with them
Saravali 22.10-11 lists a slim build, endurance of hardship and few sons
Saravali 22.10-11 mentions risk connected with water

by_area.personality: Wise, decorous and good-looking, fond of food, garlands, robes and scents (Saravali 22.10-11); clever, reflective, slow to act, self-confident, tactful and sociable (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Trade in cloth and perfumes (Brihat Jataka 18.1; Raman: dealer in perfumes); singing, instruments and dance (Saravali 22.10-11; Raman: musician).
by_area.health: Saravali 22.10-11 mentions face and eye complaints, a lean body and risk from water; treat as traditional notes, not predictions.
by_area.relationships: Brihat Jataka 18.1 and Raman say the native is at odds with or disliked by women; present only as a tradition, never as a forecast.
by_area.family: Saravali 22.10-11 gives few sons; confirm from the 5th house before mentioning.

strengtheners: Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 22.12-17: royal minister, splendour, many friends as well as foes)
Upachaya placement (3rd, 6th, 10th, 11th), where Braha (pp. 17, 51) says malefics such as the Sun give excellent results
Exalted or own sign in the navamsa, or vargottama (Braha pp. 13-14, 59-60)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saturn's aspect (Saravali 22.12-17: meanness, liaisons with older women for the Sun in Venus's signs)
Placement in a dusthana (6th, 8th, 12th); Braha (pp. 51-52) says a planet there is spoiled, the 6th being the mildest

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.1 (tr. M. D. Neely, 2007)
source_views.view: Livelihood from trade in clothing and perfumes, dislike of women, skill in singing and instrumental music.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.10-11, Sun in Taurus (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Face/eye troubles, hardship, slim, few sons, handsome, decorous, wise; enjoys food, garlands, robes and scents; skilled in song, instruments and dance; risk from water.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.12-17, aspects on the Sun in Venus's signs (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Moon: income through water-related means; Mars: bravery; Mercury: writing and song; Jupiter: ministerial posts; Venus: high status; Saturn: meanness.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 9.17 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: A planet in an enemy sign tends toward dependence on others, petty-mindedness and trouble from enemies.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.55, naisargika maitri (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1 pp. 40-41)
source_views.view: Friends are the lords of the 2nd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th and 12th from a planet's moolatrikona plus its exaltation lord; Santhanam's table gives the Sun's friends as Moon, Mars and Jupiter, enemies Venus and Saturn, and Mercury neutral.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 2.21-22 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Mercury is neutral to the Sun; Saturn and Venus are his enemies (the remaining planets, Moon, Mars and Jupiter, are friends by the verse's closing rule in 2.22).

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXII 'Planets in Different Rasis or Signs' (Sun, pp. 204-205)
source_views.view: Clever, reflective, deals in perfumes, disliked by women, slow to act, musician, self-confident, tactful, sociable.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Surya, the Sun, name 9 ('The imperishable')
source_views.view: The Sun is uncomfortable in Libra, a movable Venus sign, but not afflicted in Taurus because that fixed sign helps it stay steady.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'The Sun' p. 17, 'Navamsa' pp. 13-14, 'House Rulerships' pp. 50-52 and 'Shad Bala' pp. 59-61
source_views.view: The Sun does best in the upachaya houses and in the 10th (directional strength); planets in kendras are powerful and in trikonas flourish, while a planet in a dusthana is spoiled; dignity in the navamsa or vargottama strengthens a planet, but not a fallen one.

disagreements: Both texts agree on music, arts and enjoyment; Saravali adds bodily hardship and few sons that Brihat Jataka does not mention. Foss treats Taurus as relatively steadying for the Sun because it is a fixed sign, unlike Libra.
phrasing_guidance: Frame as artistic, steady and comfort-loving with possible friction between pride and pleasure. Do not predict problems with women, children or eyes; mention them only as traditional notes if asked.

summary: The Sun in Gemini sits in Mercury's sign, which is neutral for the Sun. Both major texts describe a learned, articulate and well-off person, skilled in calculation or astrology.
common_outcomes: Intellectual, sweet-spoken, well-mannered
Learning in both worldly and sacred subjects
Skill with numbers, writing or astrology
Comfortable finances
rare_outcomes: Saravali 22.18-19 mentions 'two mothers' (e.g. a foster or step-mother figure)
Saravali 22.18-19 notes special affection for children

by_area.personality: Sweet-spoken, well-mannered, modest and affectionate (Saravali 22.18-19); polite, critical, a good conversationalist, shy and reserved (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Astrology and learning (Brihat Jataka 18.2; Saravali 22.18-19); Raman adds astronomer, scholar and grammarian.
by_area.finance: Wealthy (Brihat Jataka 18.2; Raman); Saravali 22.18-19 adds very affluent and liberal.
by_area.family: Saravali 22.18-19: 'two mothers' (for example a foster or step-mother figure), a rare text-specific note.
by_area.spirituality: Saravali 22.18-19: expert in the shastras as well as worldly knowledge.

strengtheners: Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: knowledge of many shastras, royal messenger, foreign travel; also a fierce, bewildered temper)
Venus's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: wealth)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: loss, poverty, quarrels for the Sun in Mercury's signs)
Moon's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: trouble from kin or enemies)
Saturn's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: craftiness, though many servants)

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.2 (tr. M. D. Neely, 2007)
source_views.view: Sun in Gemini: wealthy, skilled in astrology, learned.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.18-19, Sun in Gemini (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Scholar, sweet speech, affectionate (especially to children), well-mannered, learned in worldly and sacred subjects, wealthy, generous, skilled, an astrologer, average looks, two mothers, fortunate, modest.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.20-25, aspects on the Sun in Mercury's signs (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Moon: trouble from enemies and relatives, distress abroad; Mars: fear of enemies, quarrels, poverty; Mercury: kingly history, fame, free from enemies; Jupiter: knowledge of many shastras, royal messenger, foreign travel, but fierce and bewildered; Venus: money, wife and sons; Saturn: many servants, crafty.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.55, naisargika maitri (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1 pp. 40-41)
source_views.view: Friends are the lords of the 2nd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th and 12th from a planet's moolatrikona plus its exaltation lord; Santhanam's table gives the Sun's friends as Moon, Mars and Jupiter, enemies Venus and Saturn, and Mercury neutral.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 2.21-22 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Mercury is neutral to the Sun; Saturn and Venus are his enemies (the remaining planets, Moon, Mars and Jupiter, are friends by the verse's closing rule in 2.22).

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXII 'Planets in Different Rasis or Signs' (Sun, pp. 204-205)
source_views.view: Learned, astronomer, scholarly, grammarian, polite, wealthy, critical, good conversationalist, shy and reserved, lacking originality.

disagreements: The texts agree closely. Saravali 22.20-25 gives Jupiter's aspect mixed results (learning, royal messenger work and foreign travel, but a fierce and bewildered temper), so treat that aspect result as mixed rather than simply favourable.
phrasing_guidance: Present as a bright, articulate, learning-oriented placement. Avoid promising wealth; say it supports earning through knowledge and communication.

summary: The Sun in Cancer is in the Moon's sign, a friend, but the watery, emotional sign tempers the Sun's steadiness. Texts give mixed results: honour and good qualities alongside unsteady undertakings, hard work for others and tension with relatives.
common_outcomes: Unsteady in undertakings (Saravali 22.26-27)
Works hard, often on behalf of others
Fluctuating projects or plans
Recognition for virtue, eloquence or public service
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka describes a hot-tempered, poor person who faces hardship and an austere path
Saravali 22.26-27 describes royal qualities and fame, but strain with paternal relatives and an unattractive spouse
Saravali 22.26-27 mentions study of geography or atmospheric sciences and a liking for intoxicants

by_area.personality: Unsteady in undertakings yet honourable and eloquent (Saravali 22.26-27); hot-tempered (Brihat Jataka 18.2); Raman HPA ch. XXII lists indolence, sorrow and a servile mentality.
by_area.career: Works for others (Brihat Jataka 18.2); famed for royal qualities, studies geography and the sky (Saravali 22.26-27); Raman: travelling.
by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka 18.2 and Raman say poor; Saravali 22.26-27 does not stress poverty.
by_area.health: Saravali 22.26-27 links the placement to phlegm-bile imbalance and fatigue from hard labour, and Raman lists sickliness; mention only as a traditional tendency.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 22.26-27 notes an unattractive or difficult spouse; treat cautiously and confirm from the 7th.
by_area.family: Saravali 22.26-27: hates his own people and those on the paternal side.
by_area.spirituality: Brihat Jataka 18.2 speaks of hardship on an austere path; Saravali 22.26-27: follows virtuous principles.

strengtheners: Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 22.28-33: pre-eminence) or Moon's aspect (Saravali 22.28-33: high status and water-based trade)
Mercury's aspect (Saravali 22.28-33: learning and honour)
Venus's aspect (Saravali 22.28-33: wealth through spouse)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars's aspect (Saravali 22.28-33: lung trouble and slander)
Saturn's aspect (Saravali 22.28-33: phlegm and wind disorders)

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.2 (tr. M. D. Neely, 2007)
source_views.view: Sun in Cancer: hot-tempered and poor, works for others, faces hardship on an austere path.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.26-27, Sun in Cancer (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Unsteady in undertakings yet famed for royal qualities; dislikes kin; spouse not attractive; phlegm-bile imbalance and labour; fond of intoxicants yet virtuous, honourable, eloquent; studies geography/atmosphere; steady; dislikes paternal relatives.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.28-33, aspects on the Sun in Cancer (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Moon: high status and water-trade; Mars: lung trouble and slander; Mercury: learning and honour; Jupiter: pre-eminence; Venus: wealth via spouse; Saturn: phlegm and wind complaints.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.55, naisargika maitri (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1 pp. 40-41)
source_views.view: Friends are the lords of the 2nd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th and 12th from a planet's moolatrikona plus its exaltation lord; Santhanam's table gives the Sun's friends as Moon, Mars and Jupiter, enemies Venus and Saturn, and Mercury neutral.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 2.21-22 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Mercury is neutral to the Sun; Saturn and Venus are his enemies (the remaining planets, Moon, Mars and Jupiter, are friends by the verse's closing rule in 2.22).

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXII 'Planets in Different Rasis or Signs' (Sun, pp. 204-205)
source_views.view: Poor, indolent, sorrowful, sickly, travelling, servile mentality; also lists cruelty.

disagreements: Brihat Jataka is clearly unfavourable (temper, poverty, labour for others); Saravali is mixed with notable honour and virtue. Both agree on effort, strain and some family friction.
phrasing_guidance: Say this placement mixes sensitivity and service with pride; results depend strongly on the Moon. Avoid stating poverty or a bad marriage as fact.

summary: Leo is the Sun's own sign; 0-20° is its moolatrikona and 20-30° own sign. It gives authority, courage, self-respect and a love of open, wild places, with a quick temper.
common_outcomes: Natural authority and leadership, strong self-respect
Courage and decisive action; defeats rivals
Love of nature, forests, hills and open spaces
Quick to anger; proud
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka says the native is vigorous but lacks knowledge
Saravali 22.34-35 says the native becomes a wealthy, famous ruler
Saravali 22.34-35 mentions fondness for meat

by_area.personality: Quick to anger, enthusiastic, valorous, talkative and restless (Saravali 22.34-35); vigorous (Brihat Jataka 18.2); stubborn, strong, independent and generous (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Notable deeds and kingly status (Saravali 22.34-35); Raman: organising capacity and talent for propaganda; Braha ('Planets in the Houses') gives fame and high position when the own-sign Sun is in the 10th.
by_area.finance: Saravali 22.34-35: plentiful wealth and fame; Raman: poor. The texts disagree.

strengtheners: Within 0-20° (moolatrikona) per BPHS 3.51
Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 22.36-41: builds temples, gardens and tanks; highly intelligent) or Mars's aspect (courage, leadership)
Moon's aspect (Saravali 22.36-41: scholarship, royal favour)
Kendra or trikona placement; Braha (p. 50) says planets in kendras are powerful and those in trikonas flourish
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus's aspect (Saravali 22.36-41: bad repute)
Saturn's aspect (Saravali 22.36-41: obstruction)
Mercury's aspect gives learning but Saravali also notes gambling or a mean streak
Placement in a dusthana (6th, 8th, 12th); Braha (pp. 51-52) says a planet there is spoiled, the 6th being the mildest
lagna_or_context_notes: Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the own-sign Sun house by house. With the Sun in Leo: Leo lagna (1st) respect, learning and a good start in life; Scorpio lagna (10th) fame and a high position; Aries lagna (5th) intelligence, faith and possible leadership; Gemini lagna (3rd) courage and a strong personality; Libra lagna (11th) wealth from many sources; Taurus lagna (4th) homes and property but less happiness from the mother.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.51
source_views.view: Leo 0-20° is the Sun's moolatrikona; the rest is its own sign.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.2 (tr. M. D. Neely, 2007)
source_views.view: Sun in Leo: fond of forests, mountains and cattle pens; vigorous but lacking knowledge.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.34-35, Sun in Leo (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Destroys enemies, quick-tempered, notable deeds, roams forests/hills/forts, enthusiastic, valorous, bright, eats meat, formidable, talkative, restless, wealthy and famous ruler.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 9.15 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: A planet in its own sign brings power, a stable home, property and respect among one's people during its period.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.36-41, aspects on the Sun in Leo (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Moon: scholarship, good spouse, royal favour; Mars: courage and leadership, interest in others' spouses; Mercury: scholar and writer but a gambler; Jupiter: builds temples, gardens and tanks, highly intelligent; Venus: ill repute; Saturn: creates obstacles.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXII 'Planets in Different Rasis or Signs' (Sun, pp. 204-205)
source_views.view: Stubborn, strong, poor, independent, organising capacity and talent for propaganda, humanitarian, frequents solitary places, generous; also lists cruelty.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, ch. 'The Signs: How Planets Transmit Influences of the Stars', pp. 127-128
source_views.view: Gives the Sun's moolatrikona as 4-20 degrees Leo and says planets in own sign or moolatrikona are strong.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'The Sun' p. 17 and 'Planets in the Houses' pp. 79 ff.
source_views.view: The Sun gives very good results in Leo, its own sign; gives house-by-house results for the Sun in Aries or Leo.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'The Sun' p. 17, 'Navamsa' pp. 13-14, 'House Rulerships' pp. 50-52 and 'Shad Bala' pp. 59-61
source_views.view: The Sun does best in the upachaya houses and in the 10th (directional strength); planets in kendras are powerful and in trikonas flourish, while a planet in a dusthana is spoiled; dignity in the navamsa or vargottama strengthens a planet, but not a fallen one.

disagreements: Brihat Jataka says vigour without knowledge; Saravali stresses wealth, fame and rulership; Raman calls the native poor. All agree on courage and love of wild places. BPHS 3.51-54 puts the moolatrikona at 0-20 degrees Leo; Frawley (p. 127) gives 4-20 degrees.
phrasing_guidance: Present as strong leadership and self-belief; suggest channelling pride and temper constructively. Do not promise status.

summary: The Sun in Virgo sits in Mercury's sign (neutral). Texts agree on skill in writing, painting, poetry, mathematics and music, with a gentle manner and a slighter build.
common_outcomes: Skilled in writing, arts, calculation or technical craft
Gentle, soft-spoken manner
Service to elders, teachers or the divine
Analytical, detail-oriented approach
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka and Saravali 22.42-43 describe a feminine or slight physique
Saravali 22.42-43 names skill in repairing vehicles and in Vedic study

by_area.personality: Gentle, soft and kind of speech (Saravali 22.42-43); frank, reserved, good memory and reasoning, wants praise (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Writing, painting, poetry and mathematics (Brihat Jataka 18.2); expert writer, repairer of vehicles, Vedas, song and instruments (Saravali 22.42-43); linguist, poet and mathematician (Raman).
by_area.health: Saravali 22.42-43 notes a slight build and some weakness; treat as a traditional note, not a prediction.
by_area.spirituality: Serves gods and elders (Saravali 22.42-43); learned in religious lore (Raman).

strengtheners: Mercury's or Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: knowledge of many shastras, royal messenger, foreign travel; also a fierce, bewildered temper)
Upachaya placement (3rd, 6th, 10th, 11th), where Braha (pp. 17, 51) says malefics such as the Sun give excellent results
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: loss and quarrels)
Moon's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: trouble from kin or enemies)

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.2 (tr. M. D. Neely, 2007)
source_views.view: Sun in Virgo: skilled in writing, painting, poetry and mathematics; feminine appearance.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.42-43, Sun in Virgo (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Slight, feminine build, scholarly, skilled writer, somewhat weak, serves gods and elders, skilled in repairing vehicles, Vedas, songs and instruments, soft-spoken.

summary: The Sun is debilitated in Libra (deepest fall at 10°), the sign of Venus, its enemy. Classical texts describe frustration, expenses, dependence on others and trade in metals or liquor; modern practice stresses that cancellation of debility is common and that the placement teaches cooperation over ego.
common_outcomes: Fluctuating confidence; difficulty asserting oneself
Tendency to work for or through others
Travel or residence away from home
Expenses and setbacks that require persistence

Saravali 22.44-45: dealing in gold and metals, living abroad out of distress, displeasure of authorities
Phaladeepika 9.18 (general debility): fall from position, debts, menial work, distant travel

by_area.personality: Classical verses list harsh traits (Saravali 22.44-45); Raman HPA ch. XXII gives popular, frank and submissive yet arrogant and pompous. Braha ('1st House') says a fallen Sun in the 1st undermines confidence and self-esteem, while Frawley (p. 126) says a Sun in Libra whose debility is cancelled can give a strong, self-confident, expressive character.
by_area.career: Selling liquor or working as a goldsmith (Brihat Jataka 18.3); trade in gold and metals and doing others' work (Saravali 22.44-45); Raman: manufacturer of liquors.

Debilitated planet aspected by its sign lord Venus and not in a dusthana (Phaladeepika 7.28)
Saturn, the planet exalted in Libra, in a kendra from lagna or Moon; Venus exalted; or an exalted planet joining the Sun (Braha, 'Yogas' no. 13)
Placement in an angle from lagna or Moon, the 10th most of all; at least two cancelling factors are usually needed (Frawley p. 126)
An exalted planet in Leo, the sign the Sun rules, reduces the weakness (Frawley p. 126)
Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 22.12-17: royal minister, splendour, many friends as well as foes)
Placement in the 10th, where the Sun has directional strength (Braha pp. 17, 60)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Close to 10 degrees Libra, the deepest fall (BPHS 3.49-50)
Saturn's aspect without other relief (Saravali 22.12-17: meanness, indolence, illness)
Placement in a dusthana (6th, 8th, 12th); Braha (pp. 51-52) says a planet there is spoiled, the 6th being the mildest
Vargottama does not help a fallen planet; Braha (pp. 13, 59) says it leaves it worse off
lagna_or_context_notes: Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the fallen Sun house by house. With the Sun in Libra: Libra lagna (1st) weak confidence and recognition; Leo lagna (3rd) strong but often unfulfilled desires; Cancer lagna (4th) unease and an unsettled home; Capricorn lagna (10th) a slow-to-settle career with many changes; Virgo lagna (2nd) money and family strain. Frawley (p. 126) adds that debility is much reduced in an angle from the lagna or Moon, the 10th most of all, so the Cancer, Aries, Capricorn and Libra lagna cases (4th, 7th, 10th, 1st) also carry that relief.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Surya, the Sun, name 9 ('The imperishable')

source_views.view: The Sun does best in the upachaya houses and in the 10th (directional strength); planets in kendras are powerful and in trikonas flourish, while a planet in a dusthana is spoiled; dignity in the navamsa or vargottama strengthens a planet, but not a fallen one.

disagreements: Classical sign verses are uniformly unfavourable, but Phaladeepika ch. 7, Braha and Frawley all say the debility can be cancelled, and Frawley says a cancelled Sun in Libra can be strong and self-confident. Commentators differ on whether 'lord of the exaltation sign' means Mars (lord of Aries) or Saturn (the planet exalted in Libra) (Phaladeepika 7.26 footnote); Braha lists both kinds of condition. BPHS treats all of Libra as debilitation, while Braha (p. 47) says that past 10 degrees the Sun is technically no longer fallen.
phrasing_guidance: Never call this 'bad' outright. Explain that debility is often cancelled and that the theme is building self-worth and learning cooperation. Do not repeat the texts' moral judgements or predict loss of father.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 9.16 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Friend's sign: success through friends, good spouse and children, wealth.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.50-55, aspects on the Sun in Jupiter's signs (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Moon: eloquence, wisdom, wealth and sons; Mars: fame through battle, short temper; Mercury: sweet speech, writing and arts; Jupiter: moves in royal circles, wealth and learning; Venus: refined pleasures, peace; Saturn: uncleanliness, bad company.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.55, naisargika maitri (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1 pp. 40-41)
source_views.view: Friends are the lords of the 2nd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th and 12th from a planet's moolatrikona plus its exaltation lord; Santhanam's table gives the Sun's friends as Moon, Mars and Jupiter, enemies Venus and Saturn, and Mercury neutral.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 2.21-22 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Mercury is neutral to the Sun; Saturn and Venus are his enemies (the remaining planets, Moon, Mars and Jupiter, are friends by the verse's closing rule in 2.22).

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXII 'Planets in Different Rasis or Signs' (Sun, pp. 204-205)
source_views.view: Pearl merchant, peaceful, wealthy, uneventful life, religious, prodigal, loved by women.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'The Sun' p. 17, 'Navamsa' pp. 13-14, 'House Rulerships' pp. 50-52 and 'Shad Bala' pp. 59-61
source_views.view: The Sun does best in the upachaya houses and in the 10th (directional strength); planets in kendras are powerful and in trikonas flourish, while a planet in a dusthana is spoiled; dignity in the navamsa or vargottama strengthens a planet, but not a fallen one.

disagreements: Sources agree on wealth from water; only Saravali adds untruthfulness.
phrasing_guidance: Present as a happy, prosperous, sociable placement with links to travel or water. Do not mention genital health; avoid calling the person dishonest.
